excerpt.rendered: The October 2026 issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond Magazine has arrived! Read the premier source of information on Homeschooling in South Africa

content.rendered:
Who can believe it’s already October! As the allergies kick in and the changeable weather keeps us guessing on whether to cover up or leave the house in our swimwear, we have an opportunity to mull over many of the issues confronting us in the SA Homeschooling & Beyond October 2026 issue. 

In this month’s packed issue, we take on a concern that has been surfacing in the many Facebook and WhatsApp groups around the country. A number of online schools and curriculum providers make a great case for the Cambridge curriculum.

However, many are finding that there is a knowledge gap on what it takes to get our online kids to meet South African university entrance requirements. We take a deep dive into what you need to consider and how best to direct your child’s Cambridge journey to avoid disappointment. 

As a parent of a high performance gymnastics champion, I decided to homeschool her to help balance her academic and training schedules. However, raising an elite gymnast is an expensive endeavour that also requires immense sacrifice.

Yet, parents like myself, struggle to sustain the careers in the absence of support from government and corporate South Africa. We look further into the issues affecting gymnastics parents and why wealth, not talent, determines who gets to represent their country. 

We also speak to why ECD is essential to a successful academic path for young children, and how difficult it is for matriculants in disadvantaged communities to pass. 

Happy reading and as always, your best is good enough. 

Earl Joseph

Editor-in-chief & Publisher

excerpt.rendered: The August 2026 issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond Magazine has arrived! Read the premier source of information on Homeschooling in South Africa

content.rendered:
Dear Reader

We’re into Spring and it’s the beginning of a new cycle in so many ways. You all would’ve noticed that the last few issues have been heavily focused on supporting parents of older kids, particularly matriculants. This issue would like to take a little break from the intensity of matric and turn our heads towards the little ones again. 

How many of us are aware of the emotional and cognitive loads that we carry as parents? Someone once told me that you can’t fill another’s cup when yours is empty. Kelly Eyre, Quality and Pedagogy Lead at Dibber South Africa, reminds us that when we put in the hard yards early on, we can lighten the load in your children’s later years. 

We also bring you four amazing South African children’s books that explain the world we occupy from a distinctly local perspective in the most creative ways. 

On a more serious note, more than a quarter of our children under the age of five are stunted. We take a look at how the government and private sector are working together to end stunting by 2030. 

It is also with great pride that we have partnered with EduXplore 2026, South Africa’s largest series of homeschooling events across the country. If you’re attending, pop round to our stand and say hi!

And as ever, remember that your best is good enough. 

Earl Joseph

Editor-in-chief & Publisher

content.rendered:
Dear Reader

First up, I want to share some really exciting news: SA Homeschooling & Beyond is the proud recipient of a grant from the Media Development and Diversity Agency (MDDA). This means we can expand the magazine’s scope, and reach from just homeschooling to the broader community of parents grinding away to support their children’s educational journey. Thank you MDDA!

Whether you’re helping your kids with homework after a long taxi commute, or trying to figure out what your child will do after matric, we’re here for you. Keep an eye out for exciting upgrades as we grow and expand.

This August issue lands at an important time for the matric class of 2026. Finishing school no longer means following one set path. With youth unemployment still high, the focus is turning towards resilience and practical skills.

This month’s features look at how higher learning readiness is being rethought. Kagiso Trust has launched its Makers of the Future toolkit: a free resource that helps learners cope with exam pressure and introduces them to options such as technical and vocational education and training (TVET) colleges. 

Vocational paths and structured learnerships are proving to be a strong route to economic independence by pairing classroom teaching with real workplace experience. Demand for technology skills also means digital education is now central to future job security. From coding to specialised qualifications like Inscape’s Bachelor of Design in Ideation Design, young people are learning to think for themselves rather than just memorise facts.

The high school experience is changing too. Some alternative schools now combine a structured timetable with more flexibility. Flanders Campus offers robotics and other tech-focused learning, while Praxis Education runs Independent Examinations Board (IEB) pathways through full-time campus study or a hybrid model. For families still working through university applications, we also look at public and private institutions with later registration deadlines, so options stay open a bit longer.

Always remember, your best is good enough. 

Earl Joseph

Editor-in-chief & Publisher

title.rendered: JUNE 2026 WINTER EDUCATION ISSUE OUT NOW!

excerpt.rendered: The June 2026 issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond Magazine has arrived! Read the premier source of information on Homeschooling in South Africa

content.rendered:
Welcome to the Winter Education Issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond! This month we take a deeper look into what to do to help our online schooled kids transition into mainstream tertiary education.

For those of you considering going the other way, we put together a comprehensive guide to 10 of South Africa’s online schools and which one suits your specific needs and budget. 

If your youngster is taking the IEB route, we take a detailed look at the grading system to help you help your child meet their requirements. 

As involved parents, we take our kids’ education very seriously. Yet how many of us truly understand what it means to see their education as a long-term investment? Darren Purdon of AdvTech gives us an interesting view on how to approach it as such. 

Last, but not least, Dr. Alucia Mabunda of IIE Rosebank College, explains why matric June exams are an important checkpoint in the last year of school. 

Check out the full issue and constant updates at www.sahomeschooling.com.

Enjoy!

Earl Joseph

Editor-in-chief & Publisher

content.rendered:
We’re already deep into the second term of 2026 and time for the March/April issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond. 

Inspired by my own experience of starting online homeschooling for my youngest daughter, we updated Anel van der Merwe’s excellent “Homeschooling for Beginners” guide. This issue also includes an insightful, if controversial, opinion from Karin van Oostrum of the Pestalozzi Trust on global homeschooling trends following a recent UNESCO report.

Preparing kids for university life is another focus: David Botha gives us a refresher course on how to teach our kids about financial independence. Finally, prioritize your own health with a fat loss healthy snack regime contributed by our new parent fitness coach, Dorian Apollos.

Enjoy!

Earl Joseph

excerpt.rendered: The February 2026 issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond Magazine has arrived! Read the premier source of information on Homeschooling in South Africa

content.rendered:
Welcome to the February 2026 issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond which is packed with insights we know will resonate with you. Cognitive behavioural specialist, Dalena van der Westhuizen, provides practical solutions for tackling child procrastination using simple techniques like chunking tasks and time-blocking. 

For those navigating challenging educational paths, our guide on remedial and alternative schooling by Barbara Robinson of Orion College clarifies how South African taxpayers might be eligible to claim certain related medical and school expenses. We also look to the future, with Yesh Surjoodeen of HP Southern Africa on the potential for AI education technology to bridge learning gaps across Africa. 

Beyond academics, Kelly Eyre guides us on social-emotional learning in preschoolers. She helps to reframe what can look like bullying as a learning process. Finally, we’ve included a powerful piece by George Mwaura on the role of social fathers in South Africa’s communities. We also cover child online safety and the role of the Films and Publications Board as well as a necessary, transparent update from the Pestalozzi Trust on the administrative hurdles in the BELA Act registration process.

Enjoy the read and don’t forget to Subscribe for constant updates on parenting, education and your child’s wellbeing.

Warmly,

Earl Joseph

excerpt.rendered: The 2025 Summer issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond Magazine has arrived! Read the premier source of information on Homeschooling in South Africa

content.rendered:
The Summer 2025 Issue of SA Homeschooling & Beyond is here!

It has been a truly long year, and most of us anticipate that well-deserved break. However, before we depart, there is always a final push to the finish line. Whatever is causing the scramble, it is difficult to keep all the balls in the air.

Somewhere in the rush, we must figure out how to financially afford and plan the holiday, consider next year’s homeschooling requirements as well as how to keep our children healthy after a long, food-filled holiday. This month’s magazine tackles these issues and more.

We provide tips to get ready for 2026, how to navigate Black Friday and end of year sales and a guide to physical activity for your kids. We also keep an eye on how to manage neurodivergence, particularly autistic children, and what educational options you have.

With another packed edition, you will have plenty to read on your holidays. Let us all enjoy the break, be safe, and return refreshed. Happy Holidays from the SA Homeschooling and Beyond team!

Subscribe now for more regular content on educational, parenting and developmental issues affecting you as a member of our homeschooling community. 


Regards, 


Earl Joseph

Publisher & Editor
